description: The image displays three pie charts illustrating the distribution of results across different categories for three distinct experimental conditions: “easy,” “medium,” and “Zero-Shot,” as referenced in the paper “Knowledge Crosswords: Geometric Knowledge Reasoning with Large Language Models.” Each pie chart is divided into four colored segments, corresponding to the categories labeled in the legend as N-K+ (teal), N-K- (yellow), N+K- (orange), and N+K+ (red). The “easy” chart shows the largest segment as teal (N-K+) at 55.4%, followed by yellow (N-K-) at 38.3%, and then red (N+K-) at 4.6%, with a small orange (N+K+) segment at 1.7%. The “medium” chart features the largest segment as teal (N-K+) at 58.8%, followed by yellow (N-K-) at 35.4%, then red (N+K-) at 4.0%, and a very small orange (N+K+) segment at 1.8%. The “Zero-Shot” chart shows two largest segments: yellow (N-K-) at 37.3% and orange (N+K-) at 37.9%, followed by teal (N-K+) at 18.1%, and a small red (N+K+) segment at 6.7%. Each pie chart has percentage labels directly on its respective slices, and the legend is positioned to the right, clearly associating each color with its corresponding category. The charts appear to be ordered from left to right in terms of the difficulty level of the task, with “easy” on the left, “medium” in the middle, and “Zero-Shot” on the right.
